events.title: Vue.js publicly released
events.summary: Evan You released Vue.js in February 2014 — a progressive framework extracting Angular's data binding without the weight.
events.about: Vue offers reactive data binding, single-file components, and optional routing/state (Vue Router, Pinia) — adopt incrementally on existing pages or build full SPAs. Popular in Laravel stacks, Chinese tech ecosystems, and teams wanting [React]-like ergonomics with gentler learning curve.

narrative.whyChosen: Vue became the third pillar of modern frontends alongside [React] and Angular.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved a progressive, incrementally adoptable framework could compete with all-in SPA platforms.
narrative.problemSolved: AngularJS felt heavy for quick prototypes; You wanted reactive templates and components in a small package.

events.title: OpenID Connect 1.0 published
events.summary: The OpenID Foundation published [OpenID Connect] Core 1.0 on February 25, 2014 — an identity layer on top of [OAuth] 2.0 for login and profile sharing.
events.about: [OpenID Connect] adds ID tokens (JWTs), a UserInfo endpoint, and standardized scopes to [OAuth] — `Sign in with Google` flows use it under the hood. Relying parties verify issuer, audience, and signature instead of inventing login protocols. Example: exchange an authorization code for an ID token containing `sub`, `email`, and `name` claims.

narrative.whyChosen: [OpenID Connect] standardized federated login on the [OAuth] 2.0 foundation.
narrative.whyImportant: It replaced proprietary social-login hacks with interoperable identity tokens across providers.
narrative.problemSolved: [OAuth] 2.0 alone did not define how to authenticate users or share profile data securely.

events.title: Satya Nadella named Microsoft CEO
events.summary: Microsoft's board appointed Satya Nadella CEO on February 4, 2014 — starting the cloud-first, open-source era.
events.about: Nadella accelerated Azure, open-sourced .NET, acquired GitHub, and championed VS Code and [TypeScript]. For developers, Microsoft transformed from Windows-only vendor to cross-platform tools company.

narrative.whyChosen: Nadella's appointment reversed Microsoft's developer reputation.
narrative.whyImportant: It legitimized open source inside the company that once fought Linux.
narrative.problemSolved: Microsoft was losing cloud and mobile developers to open, cross-platform stacks.

events.title: Shopify Plus launched
events.summary: Shopify announced Shopify Plus on February 4, 2014 — an enterprise e-commerce tier with dedicated support, higher [API] limits, and white-glove onboarding.
events.about: Shopify Plus extended the platform to high-volume merchants like Tesla, Budweiser, and the LA Lakers — competing with Magento Enterprise and Salesforce Commerce Cloud. It became Shopify's fastest-growing revenue segment.

narrative.whyChosen: Shopify Plus moved Shopify from SMB into enterprise e-commerce.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved hosted SaaS could serve high-traffic enterprise storefronts.
narrative.problemSolved: Fast-growing Shopify merchants outgrew standard plans but wanted to stay on the platform.

events.title: GitHub Atom editor released
events.summary: GitHub released the Atom text editor preview on February 26, 2014 — a hackable editor built on the Electron framework.
events.about: Atom brought web technologies to desktop editing: [HTML], CSS, and JavaScript for themes and packages, plus built-in Git integration. It powered GitHub's own hackable-editor pitch before VS Code won the category — and Electron became the stack for Slack, Discord, and VS Code itself.

narrative.whyChosen: Atom proved Electron could ship polished developer tools, not just chat apps.
narrative.whyImportant: It pushed the 'hackable editor' idea into mainstream open source before Microsoft's response.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers wanted a modern, extensible editor tied to Git workflows without proprietary lock-in.

events.title: Slack team messaging launches
events.summary: Stewart Butterfield's [Slack] launched publicly on February 12, 2014 — a channel-based chat app born from a failed game startup that replaced email for engineering teams.
events.about: [Slack] integrated GitHub commits, [Jira] tickets, PagerDuty alerts, and `/giphy` into searchable channels — IRC for enterprises with OAuth bots and threads. It normalized async work chat alongside Zoom standups; Salesforce acquired it for $27.7B in 2021. Developers still joke about notification overload, but [Slack] became the town square of modern software orgs.

narrative.whyChosen: [Slack] replaced internal email and IRC for millions of software teams.
narrative.whyImportant: Integrations turned chat into the notification hub for CI, deploys, and incidents.
narrative.problemSolved: Email and ad-hoc IM could not keep distributed engineering teams aligned in real time.

events.title: Monday.com work OS launched
events.summary: dapulse rebranded and launched Monday.com in February 2014 — a colorful spreadsheet-kanban hybrid for tracking projects, sprints, and marketing work.
events.about: Monday.com targeted teams that found [Jira] intimidating and Trello too simple — customizable boards with automations and integrations. It spread from startups to non-technical departments, competing with Asana and Notion for visibility into who is doing what.

narrative.whyChosen: Monday.com made visual work tracking mainstream outside pure engineering teams.
narrative.whyImportant: Its template boards lowered the bar for cross-functional project visibility.
narrative.problemSolved: Managers needed shared status views without learning [Jira] query language.
